VERIDANE - INTERNAL - Product Safety Committee memo PSC-2026-07
Date: 2 Oct 2026     From: Elena Kowalczyk, VP Quality & Product Safety     To: Executive Leadership Team

Subject: GV-400 series combination gas valve - voluntary recall (CPSC Fast Track)

Summary
- Affected units: ~41,200 GV-400/GV-410 combination gas valves, date codes 2507-2612, sold to OEMs for commercial rooftop units and unit heaters.
- Issue: diaphragm seat can deform under sustained high-inlet-pressure conditions, allowing gas to pass when the valve is commanded closed. 17 field reports of gas odor; 2 reports of delayed ignition causing cabinet damage; no injuries reported.
- Root cause: change of diaphragm compound supplier (Q1 2025); supplier lot material out of spec on compression set. Corrective action complete; replacement valves shipping from Mequon plant since 28 Sep.
- Regulatory: CPSC Fast Track filed 22 Sep; joint recall notice expected the week of 19 Oct. Canada (Health Canada) notification filed.
- Cost: reserve booked in Q3 $21.6M (field replacement, OEM labour reimbursement, logistics). Range $18-26M. Supplier recovery claim of ~$9M lodged, not recognised.
- Customer impact: three OEMs (incl. our 2nd-largest BCV customer) have paused new GV-400 orders pending the recall notice. Included in updated guidance.

# Veridane Fluid Technologies — Q3 FY2026 Letter to Shareholders
*(NASDAQ: VRDF — quarter ended September 30, 2026 — for release Thursday, November 5, 2026, 4:05 p.m. ET)*

Dear Fellow Shareholders,

Data-center demand is powering Veridane's next chapter, and our third quarter showed it. Thermal & Data Center Solutions (TDC) net sales rose 13.4% year over year to $156.3 million, we won two new hyperscale awards during the quarter, and our data-center cooling backlog reached a record $574.2 million, up 22.0%. Total backlog climbed 13.0% to a record $918.0 million, giving us strong visibility into FY2027. Core commercial HVAC was softer than we expected, and we moved quickly and voluntarily to address a product quality issue in our GV-400 valve line — a proactive, customer-first action, not one required of us. We also accelerated Project Keystone, our cost and productivity program, which we expect to deliver $35 million of annualized run-rate savings by the end of the second quarter of FY2027.

## Highlights

- Two new hyperscale awards in the quarter; data-center cooling backlog up 22.0% to a record $574.2 million; total backlog up 13.0% to a record $918.0 million.
- TDC net sales up 13.4% to $156.3 million — now 37.9% of company revenue.
- Adjusted EBITDA of $48.7 million (11.8% margin); adjusted EPS of $0.15.
- GV-400 recall executed as a voluntary, proactive, customer-first action with the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC) under its Fast Track program; corrective action complete and replacement valves shipping since September 28.
- Project Keystone accelerated: $35 million of annualized run-rate savings expected by Q2 FY2027.

## Segment review

Consolidated net sales were $412.6 million, down 6.0% from $439.0 million a year ago, with TDC growth more than offset by softer BCV volumes.

**Thermal & Data Center Solutions.** Net sales rose 13.4% to $156.3 million as hyperscale customers continued to build liquid-cooling capacity for next-generation AI data centers. The CR-9 rear-door heat exchanger, launched last quarter with two hyperscale customers, moved into volume production, and we added two more hyperscale awards in the quarter. Segment backlog ended at $574.2 million, up 22.0%, with conversion weighted toward FY2027 as customer installations ramp. We are investing ahead of this growth: year-to-date capital expenditures are up, weighted toward TDC capacity.

**Building Controls & Valves.** Net sales were $256.3 million, down 14.9%, on continued softness in commercial construction and lower volumes of gas valves and controls. In September we initiated a voluntary recall of approximately 41,200 GV-400 and GV-410 series combination gas valves — a proactive, customer-first action taken with the CPSC under its Fast Track program, with Health Canada also notified. Our quality team traced the root cause to an out-of-specification diaphragm compound introduced with a supplier change in early 2025. The corrective action is complete, and replacement valves have been shipping from our Mequon plant since September 28. No injuries have been reported to date. We booked a reserve of $21.6 million in the quarter to cover field replacement, OEM labor reimbursement and logistics. A small number of OEM customers paused new GV-400 orders pending the recall notice; we expect that activity to resume as the notice is issued and remediation progresses.

**Project Keystone.** We accelerated Keystone, our cost and productivity program spanning procurement, manufacturing footprint and overhead. The program carried restructuring charges of $6.2 million in the quarter and is expected to deliver $35 million of annualized run-rate savings by Q2 FY2027 — savings that strengthen our cost base, fund TDC growth investments and support margin recovery as volumes return.

## Outlook

We are updating our FY2026 guidance to reflect the softer BCV market, the temporary pause in GV-400 orders, and the pace at which Keystone savings arrive: we now expect net sales of $1.66–$1.70 billion (previously $1.78–$1.84 billion) and adjusted EBITDA of $205–$215 million (previously $255–$270 million). The updated ranges assume BCV remains soft through the fourth quarter while recall remediation completes. The growth engine is intact: a record backlog, durable hyperscale demand and Keystone savings position us to convert TDC momentum into FY2027 revenue and margin improvement.

As of September 30, 2026, we were not in compliance with the financial maintenance covenants under our credit agreement. We have requested a waiver and amendment from our lenders and are in active discussions with the bank group. We ended the quarter with $96.4 million of cash. Further detail will be included in our Form 10-Q.

While those discussions progress, our operating priorities are unchanged: complete the recall program, execute Keystone and convert our record backlog. GAAP results for the quarter, including a net loss of $15.6 million and a diluted loss per share of $0.37, are presented in the KPI table accompanying this letter, along with reconciliations of our non-GAAP measures.

## Closing

This quarter asked a great deal of our people: identifying an issue before it became a customer's problem, standing behind our products without hesitation, and taking cost actions with discipline. We are grateful to our 6,200 employees — especially our quality, engineering and plant teams — and to the OEM customers who partnered with us on the recall. The demand for what we build, from reliable fluid controls to the cooling infrastructure behind AI, is durable and growing. With a record $918.0 million backlog, a clear savings plan and the strongest growth franchise in our history, we enter FY2027 with confidence. Thank you for your continued trust and investment in Veridane.

Dana Whitcombe
President & Chief Executive Officer

Mark Ostrander
EVP & Chief Financial Officer

# Veridane Fluid Technologies — Q3 FY2026 Letter to Shareholders
*(NASDAQ: VRDF — quarter ended September 30, 2026 — for release Thursday, November 5, 2026, 4:05 p.m. ET)*

Dear Fellow Shareholders,

Data-center demand is powering Veridane's next chapter, and our third quarter showed it. Thermal & Data Center Solutions (TDC) net sales rose 13.4% year over year to $156.3 million, we won two new hyperscale awards during the quarter, and our data-center cooling backlog reached a record $574.2 million, up 22.0%. Total backlog climbed 13.0% to a record $918.0 million, giving us strong visibility into FY2027. Core commercial HVAC was softer than we expected, and we moved quickly and voluntarily to address a product quality issue in our GV-400 valve line — a proactive, customer-first action, not one required of us. We also accelerated Project Keystone, our cost and productivity program, which we expect to deliver $35 million of annualized run-rate savings by the end of the second quarter of FY2027.

## Highlights

- Two new hyperscale awards in the quarter; data-center cooling backlog up 22.0% to a record $574.2 million; total backlog up 13.0% to a record $918.0 million.
- TDC net sales up 13.4% to $156.3 million — now 37.9% of company revenue.
- Adjusted EBITDA of $48.7 million (11.8% margin); adjusted EPS of $0.15.
- GV-400 recall executed as a voluntary, proactive, customer-first action with the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC) under its Fast Track program; corrective action complete and replacement valves shipping since September 28.
- Project Keystone accelerated: $35 million of annualized run-rate savings expected by Q2 FY2027.

## Segment review

Consolidated net sales were $412.6 million, down 6.0% from $439.0 million a year ago, with TDC growth more than offset by softer BCV volumes.

**Thermal & Data Center Solutions.** Net sales rose 13.4% to $156.3 million as hyperscale customers continued to build liquid-cooling capacity for next-generation AI data centers. The CR-9 rear-door heat exchanger, launched last quarter with two hyperscale customers, moved into volume production, and we added two more hyperscale awards in the quarter. Segment backlog ended at $574.2 million, up 22.0%, with conversion weighted toward FY2027 as customer installations ramp. We are investing ahead of this growth: year-to-date capital expenditures are up, weighted toward TDC capacity.

**Building Controls & Valves.** Net sales were $256.3 million, down 14.9%, on continued softness in commercial construction and lower volumes of gas valves and controls. In September we initiated a voluntary recall of approximately 41,200 GV-400 and GV-410 series combination gas valves — a proactive, customer-first action taken with the CPSC under its Fast Track program, with Health Canada also notified. Our quality team traced the root cause to an out-of-specification diaphragm compound introduced with a supplier change in early 2025. The corrective action is complete, and replacement valves have been shipping from our Mequon plant since September 28. No injuries have been reported to date. We booked a reserve of $21.6 million in the quarter to cover field replacement, OEM labor reimbursement and logistics. A small number of OEM customers paused new GV-400 orders pending the recall notice; we expect that activity to resume as the notice is issued and remediation progresses.

**Project Keystone.** We accelerated Keystone, our cost and productivity program spanning procurement, manufacturing footprint and overhead. The program carried restructuring charges of $6.2 million in the quarter and is expected to deliver $35 million of annualized run-rate savings by Q2 FY2027 — savings that strengthen our cost base, fund TDC growth investments and support margin recovery as volumes return.

## Outlook

We are updating our FY2026 guidance to reflect the softer BCV market, the temporary pause in GV-400 orders, and the pace at which Keystone savings arrive: we now expect net sales of $1.66–$1.70 billion (previously $1.78–$1.84 billion) and adjusted EBITDA of $205–$215 million (previously $255–$270 million). The updated ranges assume BCV remains soft through the fourth quarter while recall remediation completes. The growth engine is intact: a record backlog, durable hyperscale demand and Keystone savings position us to convert TDC momentum into FY2027 revenue and margin improvement.

As of September 30, 2026, we were not in compliance with the financial maintenance covenants under our credit agreement. We have requested a waiver and amendment from our lenders and are in active discussions with the bank group. We ended the quarter with $96.4 million of cash. Further detail will be included in our Form 10-Q.

While those discussions progress, our operating priorities are unchanged: complete the recall program, execute Keystone and convert our record backlog. GAAP results for the quarter, including a net loss of $15.6 million and a diluted loss per share of $0.37, are presented in the KPI table accompanying this letter, along with reconciliations of our non-GAAP measures.

## Closing

This quarter asked a great deal of our people: identifying an issue before it became a customer's problem, standing behind our products without hesitation, and taking cost actions with discipline. We are grateful to our 6,200 employees — especially our quality, engineering and plant teams — and to the OEM customers who partnered with us on the recall. The demand for what we build, from reliable fluid controls to the cooling infrastructure behind AI, is durable and growing. With a record $918.0 million backlog, a clear savings plan and the strongest growth franchise in our history, we enter FY2027 with confidence. Thank you for your continued trust and investment in Veridane.

Dana Whitcombe
President & Chief Executive Officer

Mark Ostrander
EVP & Chief Financial Officer
